Issued at 1046 PM MDT Thu Oct 8 2026

UNSEASONABLY WARM WEATHER CONTINUES THROUGH FRIDAY:

High pressure sitting to our west will continue to lead to 
drier and unseasonably warm conditions through Friday. Daytime 
heating and instability will lead to some terrain based showers 
and storms Friday afternoon once again, but weak steering winds 
and lack of shear will lead to pop and drop variety with gusty 
winds possible. High temperatures will once again be near 
records with highs 10 to 15 degrees above normal.

WET THIS WEEKEND:

The big story to watch is the potential moisture increase this 
weekend with the remnants of Tropical Storm Rachel working 
through the Desert Southwest. Tropical Storm Rachel currently is
sitting well off the coast of the Baja but is forecast to make 
landfall somewhere near the northern tip of the Baja and SoCal 
by Sunday morning. A deep low pressure trough descending down 
the west coast from the Pacific Northwest on Saturday will help 
steer TS Rachel inland and pull the tropical moisture through 
the Great Basin in the SW flow from the deepening trough. 
Models are coming into better agreement on the timing of this 
deep moisture push with PWAT anomalies increasing to 200-250 
percent of normal by Saturday afternoon with the biggest push 
Saturday night into Sunday as PWAT anomalies climb to near 300 
percent of normal with the ECMWF being the wetter of the models 
compared to the GFS. Given the timing of this moisture push, we 
could see more abundant cloud cover by Saturday morning. Showers
look to develop Saturday morning with scattered coverage by 
Saturday afternoon. Showers will become widespread by Saturday 
evening into Sunday. There is some uncertainty with regards to 
storm type as we could see more stratiform rainfall with 
embedded thunderstorms given the abundance of moisture and 
timing with more cloud cover in place. We will have jet support 
by Sunday so if we see any breaks in the cloud cover, we could 
see some stronger storms develop, which could lead to heavier 
rainfall rates and localized flash flooding concerns as well as 
quick rises along streams and rivers. At this time, it appears 
like the higher rainfall totals through Sunday are focused 
across eastern Utah, mainly the eastern Uintas and southwest 
Colorado over the San Juans and adjacent valleys where 1 to 2 
inches of rainfall is possible, but this could change depending 
on the track of Rachel. We will have a clearer picture once hi-
res guidance comes in.

Another concern given the proximity of the jet is stronger 
winds across eastern Utah and western Colorado Sunday afternoon 
and especially late in the day on Sunday as models are hinting 
at a dry slot which could potentially lead to some breaks in the
cloud cover and stronger winds mixing down as well as stronger 
storm potential. Current projections have wind gusts 30 to 50 
mph in the realm of possibilities. 

COOLER, CONTINUED WET WEATHER NEXT WEEK:

Beyond this weekend, forecast confidence is lower. As the 
remnants of TS Rachel exit to the northeast, another tropical 
system, Hurricane Simon, will approach the west-central coast 
of Mexico and is projected to move inland Sunday into Monday. 
Whether we get this moisture or not depends on the development 
and track of the aforementioned deepening trough to our west 
which looks to carve out a closed upper low over the Great 
Basin. The combination of this closed low to our west and high 
pressure over SE Texas continue to steer the moisture from the 
remnants of Simon well east of our area. Meanwhile, this closed 
low looks to pack a punch as a stronger jet develops early next 
week resulting in some breezy afternoons before the low tracks 
across eastern Utah and western Colorado Tuesday into Wednesday.
We can still expect daily showers and storms as moisture and 
forcing remain present. A cold front associated with this system
will cause a notable drop in temperatures and snow levels, 
leading to increasing chances for mountain snow, especially 
above 10,000 feet. So this system could lead to some decent snow
accumulations in the mountains with high temperatures dropping 
to 5 to 10 degrees below normal by Wednesday. This is a very 
fluid forecast and we expect the details to change between now 
and next week. For now, be aware that rapidly changing weather 
conditions are possible next week.
